page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T25 processors running at a baseline clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates with zero discrete GPUs and includes 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

This instance configuration omits bundled local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external block storage volumes for persistent data. The compute-centric hardware ratio emphasizes raw processing capacity while minimizing allocation costs associated with excess memory or local NVMe arrays. This density delivers high CPU utilization per node, though workloads dependent on large in-memory footprints or hardware accelerator acceleration are constrained by the 64.0 GB RAM boundary and absence of GPU silicon.

The hardware allocation profile of the Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.8xlarge makes it suitable for compute-heavy applications that do not require dedicated graphics hardware or onboard storage. Primary target workloads include compute-intensive batch processing, software compilation, CI/CD execution, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.
